meta.name: RevenueForge Brain Refactor — Consulting-Led Pivot
meta.purpose: Persisted roadmap for refactoring the RevenueForge Notion brain from a product-led Revenue OS firm to a consulting-led Fractional Chief AI Revenue Officer (CAIRO) model. Each item is debated 1-by-1 via /expert-debate before any Notion edit. Source of truth so the plan survives context compaction.

model_shift.from: Product-led: guess 3 products (Dashboard, Call Grader, CreativeIQ, Vigil), build them, charge setup + software-maintenance MRR. Moat = Vigil's compounding data.
model_shift.to: Consulting-led: Fractional Chief AI Revenue Officer. Diagnose revenue-ops AI gaps, build custom sales/marketing AI workflows, ride a build-driven retainer ($8-25k/mo) + maintenance floor. Productize via Rule of 3. Moat = operator credibility + cross-client fix-efficacy library + the factory.
model_shift.scope_discipline: Anchored in SALES & MARKETING / revenue workflows only — not generic any-AI builds. Finite, recurring problem surface; ~70% workflow reuse across clients.
model_shift.productization_gate: RULE OF 3 — the moment the same workflow is requested by a 3rd client, it exits custom and enters the productization queue. Gut gets no vote.
model_shift.positioning: Fractional Chief AI Revenue Officer (CAIRO) — the AI+Revenue intersection. Not a non-technical CRO, not a generalist CAIO. An AI-native revenue operator who builds the systems.

cross_cutting_decisions.decision: Brand name — stay 'RevenueForge' with CAIRO as positioning underneath, or rename?
cross_cutting_decisions.resolution: Company name stays RevenueForge. CAIRO (Fractional Chief AI Revenue Officer) is the disposable positioning wrapper on top — if 'AI' dates, drop it without touching the brand.

cross_cutting_decisions.decision: ICP range — brain says $2-20M, new notes say $5-50M. Confirm $5-50M?
cross_cutting_decisions.resolution: $5-20M CORE, $3M hard floor, $25M soft ceiling. $5-50M is dead. Range DERIVED not guessed: floor = $10k/mo affordability (below $3M founder IS the revenue function); ceiling = 'lean' story stops landing + internal RevOps appears ~$20-25M. Definition moved from size-first to SITUATION-first (founder-led, lean team 3-15 reps, no internal RevOps/AI, founder feels behind on AI, can pay ~$10k/mo).

cross_cutting_decisions.decision: Naming collision — Vigil / Argus / 'persistent agent layer' are 3 names for ~1 thing. Pick one.
cross_cutting_decisions.resolution: Name = Vigil (Lloyd confirmed 2026-06-29: 'Vigil is fine'). 'Argus' + 'persistent agent layer' retire as the product name. NOTE: the NAME is locked but the full product REPOSITIONING (Vigil as the future platform layer the consulting reveals demand for) is still Debate #9. Quarantined 'Vigil' refs in page changelogs stay (historical/correct); live generic 'agent layer' descriptors in Pricing Tier 2 + Business Strategy switching-costs get formally named Vigil during Debate #9.

cross_cutting_decisions.decision: FRONT DOOR = PAID AUDIT (not a free lead magnet, not a disguised sales call). Reverses Debate #7's 'free pre-sale audit'. Locked by Lloyd 2026-08-12 (podcast-driven), incl. the two-fork DIY/DFY outcome model.

model.front_door: Paid Revenue Audit. Price LADDERS: START $497, target ~$1,000 as lead-quality + positioning improve. The price itself filters tire-kickers and creates a micro-commitment that lifts audit->build conversion.
model.funnel_ladder: FREE webinar/content -> PAID $497 audit (diagnosis + roadmap) -> RECURRING build retainer (setup + MRR). Webinar is the free top-of-funnel; NO separate free mini-audit (would cannibalize the paid one). [Lloyd agreed to the folding, which included this; treat as accepted.]
model.audit_is_not_a_pitch: Genuine deep-dive diagnosis, not a disguised sales call. Honesty test: the roadmap must be worth $497 even if they never hire us. That is what makes the guarantee safe to give.

package.prework: Connect CRM + short intake form -> feeds the automated scan (Engine A from Debate #7).
package.call: 60-90 min live deep-dive = Engine B strategic diagnostic (TAM, coverage, method, marketing/demand-gen, conversion). This IS the 'sales call that isn't a sales call'.
package.deliverable: Written Revenue Gap Report + Build Roadmap: current-state map of revenue process; AI-adoption scorecard by function; prioritized gaps each mapped to a Machine Library machine or net-new; QUANTIFIED opportunity per gap (hrs saved / payroll $ / revenue unlock) = the math backing the guarantee; sequenced build roadmap; the two-fork proposal.
package.guarantee: If the report can't identify >=10 hrs/wk exec time OR $5-10k/mo payroll OR a credible revenue unlock (+10% close or lead vol), full $497 refund. Criteria pre-stated IN WRITING so a refund is a clean yes/no, never a subjective fight. Framing LEADS WITH revenue unlock (ICP is growth-driven); time/payroll savings are the secondary hook.
package.credit: $497 CREDITS toward the build/setup if they proceed (removes 'wasted money' fear, lifts conversion, reframes audit as step 1 of the engagement). Recommended yes; treat as accepted under Lloyd's 'agree with everything' unless he reverses.

two_fork_outcome.fork_A_self_deploy_DIY: They can take the roadmap and deploy it themselves. Makes $497 honest + standalone-valuable, and requires no further spend to get an outcome. Serves as the TRUST / VALUE anchor.
two_fork_outcome.fork_B_we_build_DFY: '...or we just do this for you' — faster, and they lack the time + technical depth. Where the enterprise value lives. THE TARGET outcome.
two_fork_outcome.IP_BOUNDARY_LOCKED: DIY roadmap gives DIRECTION ONLY — strategy, gaps, sequence, expected ROI, and WHICH machine solves each gap. It does NOT include the build IP: build specs, prompts, integration playbooks, or the configured system. Diagnosis is SOLD ($497); construction is RETAINED (retainer). Consistent with the Machine Library rule (spec library = internal IP). Lloyd confirmed 2026-08-12: 'DIY gives direction, not our IP.'
two_fork_outcome.cannibalization_protection: ICP self-selects toward Fork B: lean-team founder, no in-house AI skill, feels behind on AI, can pay $10k/mo -> DIY is rarely rational for them. Those who'd actually DIY are out-of-ICP (sub-$3M, can't afford us). DIY fork costs ~nothing, buys large trust.
two_fork_outcome.selling_stance: SHOW both forks (DIY visible = proof it wasn't a paid pitch). Keep INTERNAL that the whole audit is architected so Fork B is the obvious conclusion. Deliver pure diagnosis; let the prospect ARRIVE at DFY themselves rather than being pitched. Lloyd: 'more for us to internally know, we don't necessarily have to tell them that immediately.'

model.delegation_bottleneck_flag: OPEN — NOT YET RULED. At $497 with Lloyd personally running 90-min deep-dives + bespoke roadmaps, the audit does NOT scale and re-inserts Lloyd as the bottleneck (the exact thing Debate #4 fought). $497 isn't the profit — the build retainer is; the audit should ~wash its own time-cost as a qualified-lead generator. REQUIRED fix: delegatable shell — Engine A automated CRM scan + a trained team member runs intake + the data pass; Lloyd joins only for the constraint-read + roadmap framing. DECISION STILL NEEDED: accept the audit must be delegatable from day one, or run them himself while volume is low?

page_impact.7-audit: Reverse free->paid $497; add package + two-fork + guarantee + IP boundary. Two-engine design (Engine A CRM scan + Engine B strategic diagnostic) STAYS — it becomes HOW the paid audit is delivered.
page_impact.3-pricing: Add front-door tier 'Audit — $497' above the Pilot; credits toward build; Fork A (roadmap + optional coaching) & Fork B (retainer) = the two pricing paths already in the model.
page_impact.8-gtm: Webinar REWRITE: the close sells the $497 audit (not a free call); the two-fork promise ('deploy it yourself or have us do it') is the risk-reversal; funnel ladder as above.
page_impact.6-objections: Add 'why pay for an audit?' (guarantee kills it) + 'why hire you to build if you already gave me the roadmap?' (time + skill + speed + the build-IP is NOT in the map).

debate_outcome.lead: Proof-first, not title-first. Open with the operator result ('CRO of a multi-million-dollar B2B firm, doubled close rate, cut 30% off time-to-close'), THEN name the role. CAIRO is packaging + price-anchoring, not the claim.
debate_outcome.differentiated_combo: Operator who personally carried the revenue number + a real build team. Not a non-technical CRO, not a dev shop, not a generalist CAIO. The seam between diagnosis and delivery is the moat.
debate_outcome.team_value_prop: You are not buying Lloyd's hours. You are buying: Lloyd (diagnosis + architecture + sales) + dev team (Geri/Nico delivery) + the factory (productizes both the builds AND the diagnosis).
debate_outcome.two_tier_promise: Buy the operator now (fractional CAIRO running your revenue-AI), grow into the installed system later.
debate_outcome.moat: Cross-client revenue-gap -> AI-fix -> dollar-result library. Each engagement makes the diagnosis sharper and the next build faster.
debate_outcome.bottleneck_named: Lloyd's diagnosis + architecture throughput is the real ceiling (not 'team'). Escape hatch = productize the diagnosis via the Revenue Intelligence Audit so it scales beyond Lloyd's hours.

roadmap_items.change: Range $2-20M -> $5-50M. Problem reframes from 'revenue visibility gap' -> 'want to be AI-forward across revenue ops, dont know how.' 5-gap checklist (manual BD, manual content, no metrics, weak rep feedback, digital footprint) becomes diagnostic surface.

debate_outcome.range: $5-20M core, $3M floor, $25M soft ceiling (derived from $10k/mo affordability floor + 'lean' ceiling). $5-50M killed.
debate_outcome.definition: SITUATION-first not size-first: founder-led B2B, lean team 3-15 reps, no internal RevOps/AI function, founder feels behind on AI, can comfortably pay ~$10k/mo.
debate_outcome.proof_model: Dogfooding arc = proof of METHOD not a fixed menu. Prospect gaps match ours (existing asset) or differ (custom). Audit routes most to known assets; custom is the exception; Rule of 3 promotes recurring custom into assets.
debate_outcome.scope_discipline_reminder: Always 'revenue/sales/marketing problems' never generic 'business problems' (Lloyd caught himself drifting generic in debate).
debate_outcome.disqualifier_REVERSED: OLD: 'lead gen is the constraint = disqualify (infra converts, doesnt create demand)'. NEW: gap surface expanded to include top-of-funnel (automated SDR, outreach personalization, AEO/SEO footprint), so weak lead flow is NOT auto-disqualifying. LLOYD CONFIRMED the reversal. Final framing: NOT a demand disqualifier at all -- it's SCOPE. Lead gen is IN scope. Only true non-fits: (1) not a revenue/sales/marketing problem (generic 'business problems' = generalist shop, not us -- scope discipline IS the moat), (2) can't afford ~$10k/mo, (3) no working revenue motion at all to amplify (rare PMF problem). Model: 'build whatever AI solves their revenue problems, menu-first, custom only when novel.' Margin guardrail: audit routes most to menu items; custom is the exception; Rule of 3 promotes recurring custom into menu.

debate_outcome.three_tiers: Tier 0 PILOT: 3-month commitment, $8k/mo min = $24k upfront min (front door, no standalone audit SKU, filters ICP + buys runway to ship a result). Tier 1 BUILD: $8-15k/mo while actively consulting+architecting+building; revenue-dense + time-dense; LLOYD-BOTTLENECKED by design (constraint is Lloyd/Geri diagnosis+architecture throughput, not dev capacity) so run only a few concurrently. Tier 2 FLOOR/PLATFORM: $2-3k/mo PRICE-DISCOVERY ANCHOR (not final); software access + compounding agent layer; VALUE-priced not cost-priced; near-zero marginal cost, high margin-per-hour; the scalable annuity.
debate_outcome.cliff_fix: Portfolio/oscillation model. Two layers not one. Clients descend to floor (healthy, the annuity working) and RE-EXPAND into builds when the continuous-diagnosis pulse surfaces a build-worthy gap. NRR>100% via re-expansion. The ONLY enemy is churn OFF the floor -- delivery should orient around floor retention, not keeping builds artificially alive.
debate_outcome.stickiness: Systems delivered as software layers client uses daily; cancelling = losing the systems + the agent layer's accumulated history/calibration. 'Maintenance' = keeping access. Longer they stay, more it has learned, more expensive to leave.
debate_outcome.geri_partner: Geri treated as business PARTNER not contractor. Target pitch ~65-70% Lloyd / ~30-35% Geri PROFIT-SHARE. NOT YET NEGOTIATED. Future expenses (e.g. Nico/devs) deducted from partnership before split. Dev cost beyond two founders unknown. -> Debate #11.

debate_outcome.experts: Hormozi (attack: menu-first is a slogan, not enforced) + Horowitz (defend: the sequence enforces it) + Goldratt as devil's-advocate third voice (Lloyd-requested), who found the key flaw.
debate_outcome.goldratt_flaw: v1 spine put Lloyd in TWO steps (Diagnose + Architect), contradicting the Business Strategy escape-hatch claim ('standardize the audit so it scales beyond Lloyd's hours'). v1 standardized the FORMAT of the audit, not the LABOR. Throughput capped because the constraint appeared twice and nothing was subordinated to protect it.
debate_outcome.fix: Split each Lloyd-step into a delegatable shell + irreducible core. Diagnose = team/automated data-collection+scoring (no Lloyd). Route = auto-map + Lloyd 20-min review of novel gaps only. Architect = menu specs self-served from a spec library + Lloyd authors custom specs ONLY when novelty gate fires. Result: Lloyd's hours scale SUB-LINEARLY with client count.
debate_outcome.spine: 7 steps: 1 Diagnose (standardized audit surface, scored gap-cards) | 2 Route + novelty gate (auto-map to menu; Lloyd judges novel only) | 3 Architect (library self-serve for menu; Lloyd custom only) | 4 Build sprint (factory builds to spec + acceptance criteria; QA = criteria sign-off, Lloyd inspects only failures/net-new) | 5 Train/adopt (team-run, usage thresholds, HAS TEETH because un-adopted build = churn off floor = the only enemy) | 6 Re-diagnose/expand (pulse re-runs, drives oscillation/NRR>100%) | 7 Rule-of-3 ratchet (3rd custom recurrence -> templatize into library).
debate_outcome.governing_principle: Lloyd's hours-per-client must trend DOWN quarter over quarter even as client count rises. If not, the spine is broken; fix is always 'templatize more,' never 'Lloyd works more.'
debate_outcome.the_factory: Dev team (Geri+Nico/contract) building against Lloyd's specs. Spec library = the factory's input. Spec w/ acceptance criteria = the QA contract (defines 'done' before a dev starts). Scale by adding devs; Lloyd's judgment spent only on routing novel gaps + authoring custom specs.
debate_outcome.survived_repointed: Consulting=R&D (fix-efficacy record captured at Step 5), continuous-value-not-a-black-box (now structural not a 4-deliverable script), SOP-as-training-data (= the standardized audit + spec library).

pre_decisions.entry_framing_decision: DELIVERABLE-AMBIGUITY RESOLVED as a sequenced hybrid. ENTRY = use-case-anchored (Model A): content seduces prospects into a SPECIFIC machine they saw (Call Grader/DealForge/Dashboard); the quick win is deploying that machine (library deploy = fast/high-margin). ENGAGEMENT = operator-anchored (Model B): continuous-diagnosis pulse converts a one-machine buyer into an embedded-operator relationship. RISK: Model-A churn trap (buy the machine, it ships, they leave). FIX (write into this audit page): the free pre-sale audit must surface 2-3 ADDITIONAL gaps beyond the one they came for, so machine #2 is identified+sold before machine #1 ships. The use case is the hook; the audit is the multi-machine-relationship converter. This protects the annuity while keeping use-case-led entry.
